title: Strong and trustworthy
hookLine: the best to hire is the strong and the trustworthy (28:26)
carry: the kind of job nobody will check

cards: Every hiring manager has a list: experience, references, a good interview. Musa has none of it. He's a fugitive with no money, no letters, no home, sitting in a stranger's house in Madyan.
He has told the old man his whole story, and the old man has said, don't be afraid, you've escaped from the wrongdoing people. Then one of the daughters speaks up and gives him a reference.
Two words, and she has seen him earn both.

teach.b: Hire him, she tells her father. Pickthall: "the best (man) that thou canst hire is the strong, the trustworthy." In Arabic, al-qawiyy al-amin.
Qawiyy is strong, able to do the work. Amin is trustworthy, from the same root as amana, a trust, and iman, faith. She has seen both.
Strength at the well, where he watered a whole flock that had been waiting behind the shepherds.

teach.h: TRUST SEEN ON THE WALK HOME.
teach.b: Trustworthiness on the way home: commentators tell, from a report attributed to 'Umar, that Musa asked her to walk behind him and call out the way, so he wouldn't be looking at her as she walked.
That detail is from commentary, not the verse. Either way, she'd watched him work, and watched him behave when no one else was looking.
Both words matter. Strength without trust is a danger: a capable person you can't rely on. Trust without strength is a disappointment: a good person who can't do the job.

The same pair turns up once more, in Surah An-Naml, from an unlikely mouth: a jinn offering to fetch the Queen of Sheba's throne says he is strong and trustworthy for the job. The old man takes his daughter's advice.
He offers Musa marriage to one of his daughters, for eight years of work, or ten if he chooses. Musa answers: whichever term I complete, let there be no injustice to me.
A contract between two people who each had reason to trust the other. A hadith in Bukhari warns that when trust is lost, the Hour is near.

how: Muslims often cite 28:26 when speaking of hiring, leadership and work ethic, holding that a person given a role should be both capable and trustworthy.

o: trustworthy, safe to trust with the work
a stranger given shelter by a family

games.q: strong and trustworthy — tap the pairs.
p: strong, able to do the work
trustworthy, from the root of amana

s: the daughter recommends Musa for his wealth and family
he had nothing; she recommends him as strong and trustworthy.
amin shares a root with amana and iman
trustworthy, a trust, and faith all come from a-m-n.
the verse says Musa asked her to walk behind him
that detail comes from commentary, a report attributed to 'Umar.

games.q: you're the old man in Madyan. a stranger with nothing is at your table, and your daughter says, hire him. what do you do?
o: take her advice, and offer him work and marriage.
thank him and send him on.
games.why: he offers Musa one of his daughters in marriage for eight years' work, or ten if Musa chooses, and Musa agrees.

practice: Think of the work in front of you today, paid or unpaid: a job, a class, a household, caring for someone.

Ask honestly where you're strong but not quite trustworthy, a corner cut, a promise let slide, and where you're trustworthy but not yet strong. If you pray, you can ask for strength and trust together.

wordCard.voice: Al-amin. The daughter's word for Musa: trustworthy, safe to trust with the work. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the strong, the trustworthy; the daughter's words for Musa in 28:26.

carryVoice: Your line: the kind of job nobody will check. Trust shows when no one is watching. See you tomorrow, then.
